key_insight: RetiJev directly scores predefined answers, improving ophthalmic guideline-grading accuracy over larger-model baselines while avoiding autoregressive generation.
clinical_relevance: Faster ophthalmic decision support could reduce inference delays, but benchmark performance does not establish safety or benefit in clinical practice.
method: Built source-grounded training data from PubMed Central articles, an eye-disease vocabulary, and 11 guideline-grading systems.
Developed 0.8B–9B models that score candidate answers without autoregressive decoding.
Compared accuracy and inference speed with a 27B LLM and the commercial Jev 1.13 decision model.
evidence_signal: The corpus includes 78,158 clinical-decision and diagnosis questions plus 50,074 grading questions; evaluation used a 24,662-question benchmark, with grading gains of 10.4–23.0 points over baselines and RetiJev-9B inference of 158 ms per case on one GPU.
watch_item: The abstract reports no prospective clinical validation, so real-world generalizability, safety, and privacy require further assessment.
paper_title: RetiJev: Fast and Source-Grounded Ophthalmic Decision Models
